observations:
LM2 Torah 35 is a single-sentence teaching and does not yield any independent packages.

The teaching states that Torah scholars are worthy to know the future, deriving this from Psalms 119 ('I knew beforehand' — from Your testimonies, namely from the Torah). The entire content is one causal proposition: Torah learning enables foreknowledge.

For a new package to be proposed, three or more concepts must be connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. This Torah has:
  - Zero occurrences of the word 'בְּחִינַת'
  - One exegetical gloss equating עֵדוּת (testimony) with תוֹרָה (Torah)
  - No network of bechina relationships among multiple concepts

The one interpretive equation (testimony = Torah) is a borderline bechina candidate — it could, under generous reading, be recorded as a single pair in the dataset (reference 1035, type 'bechina', עֵדוּת ↔ תוֹרָה). But even if that pair were entered, two nodes and one edge fall well below the threshold of 3+ concepts forming an independent domain that would justify a new package designation.

The teaching's conceptual core — that Torah study grants prophetic foreknowledge — is captured in the existing Torah network as an eitza relationship (Torah study → access to future/דַּעַת), not as a bechina cluster.

Recommendation: If the dataset is extended to cover this Torah, enter the single borderline pair {עֵדוּת ↔ תוֹרָה} with type 'bechina' and reference 1035. Revisit package formation only if additional bechina edges are discovered in other manuscript versions or commentaries.
